title: Canonical quotient, square map and derived Hom boundary for a two-term complex
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and choose its derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ with localization $Q$ and shifts [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For objects $M,F$ and a morphism $d:M\to F$, let $K(d)=\operatorname{Cone}(d[0])$, the complex $[M\xrightarrow{d}F]$ in degrees $-1,0$. Define its positive quotient $q_d:QK(d)\to M[1]$ to be the image of the negative of the third arrow of Mathlib's cone triangle, followed by the canonical isomorphism commuting $Q$ with shift; thus its component on the shifted source is the positive projection. For $G\in\mathcal A$, define the additive boundary map $\partial_{d,G}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(QK(d),G[1])$ by $\phi\mapsto\phi[1]\circ q_d$, using the degree-zero embedding before shifting. For another $d':M'\to F'$ and maps $a:M\to M'$, $b:F\to F'$ satisfying $b\circ d=d'\circ a$, define the chain map $K(d)\to K(d')$ to be the canonical cone map with components $a$ in degree $-1$ and $b$ in degree $0$. These are explicit maps; no exactness or naturality theorem is asserted.
